title: remember_feedback_id rewrites feedback.ids with no lock or atomic replace, so two hook processes can drop an id
goal: remember_feedback_id writes feedback.ids under a lock or by an atomic replace, so the async capture hook and the MCP server recording at once keep both ids. Found by the SP-ficl7pxl review (ST-vpwkr76k gate g1).

run: import sys;s=open("_tools/ql_capture.py").read();i=s.find("def remember_feedback_id");b=s[i:s.find("\ndef ",i+10)];sys.exit(0 if "lock" in b.lower() or "os.replace" in b else 1)

repro_reason: the lost id needs two processes interleaving the read and the write; the race is not reproducible on demand, so the repro reads that the function takes no lock and no atomic replace yet

run:
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, pathlib
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); (pathlib.Path(d) / 'spool').mkdir()
c = 'import sys,pathlib;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import ql_capture as q\nfor i in range(40): q.remember_feedback_id(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])/"spool","FB-%02d%06d"%(int(sys.argv[2]),i))'
ps = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', c, d, str(k)]) for k in range(4)]
[p.wait(timeout=120) for p in ps]
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import ql_capture as q
got = set(q.written_feedback_ids(pathlib.Path(d) / 'spool')); print('ids kept', len(got), 'of 160'); sys.exit(0 if len(got) == 160 else 1)
